answer: In the hundred-year-slice PCA of the 12 forms of capital (39 slices, BCE 4300–500), the three symbolic-capital variables form a coherent positive group on PC1 but fan out along PC2. On PC1, which captures 31.8% of the variance, all three load positively and moderately — hatchets/swords +0.570 (5th of 12 by |loading|), daggers +0.529 (6th), house size +0.431 (10th) — so they cluster on the positive side of PC1 without dominating it (PC1 is led by copper/gold +0.754, pottery decoration +0.720, pottery form −0.673, and depot +0.658). Across PC2, which captures 20.4% of the variance, the three are differentiated rather than clustered: house size carries the largest PC2 loading of the three (+0.551, 5th of 12), while daggers (+0.181, 8th) and especially hatchets/swords (+0.101, 12th, essentially zero) load weakly — i.e., PC2 separates house size from the two weapon types. The "distribution across PC2" is best read as a static loading contrast (house size vs. the two weapons) rather than a monotonic early→late temporal gradient: PC2 scores are not a clean time axis (PC2 score vs BCE r≈0.04), and per-slice PC2 scores peak in the Mesolithic (≈3400–3000 BCE, maximum at 3200 BCE) and are lowest in the Early Neolithic and Young Bronze Age, with the weapon variables' own values rising through the Late Neolithic/Old Bronze Age (daggers up to +3.33 at 1800 BCE; hatchets/swords up to +2.95 at 1500 BCE) before falling again. (Loadings are reported with the PC1 sign fixed so its largest-magnitude variable, copper/gold, is positive; all loading signs are convention-dependent up to a component flip.)

payload.workflow: Loaded data/capital.csv (parsed European comma decimals; dropped group/color) -> 39 hundred-year slices x 12 standardized Z capital forms (BCE 4300-500). Ran correlation-matrix PCA via numpy SVD (sklearn unavailable) on the existing Z-values (no re-standardization, per approved A1). Computed EVR, structure-coefficient loadings (corr of each variable with each PC), per-slice PC1/PC2 scores, and per-slice values + PC2-weighted contributions of the three symbolic variables (Zhausgr, ZDolch, ZAxtSchwert). Fixed PC1/PC2 sign so the largest-|loading| variable is positive. Ranked all 12 variables on both axes by |loading|. Saved loading table, per-slice score table, and eigenvalues as artifacts.
